messages.subject: Including additional phenotypes of un-genotyped individuals
messages.subject_clean: Including additional phenotypes of un-genotyped individuals
messages.body_plain:

Is there a easy way to add phenotypes of individuals that were not selected for genotyping to stratify my scanone/scan1 permutation test (as per Manichaikul 2007)? The only way I can think is to add the phenotypes and missing data pre-read.cross (in shell), or to manually add into the cross object.
Any help is much appreciated!
Jeff

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] funny scantwo p-values
messages.body_plain:
The p-values are the proportion of permutation replicates with LOD scores >= the observed.
So if no permutations gave that big of a LOD score, the p-value will be 0.
If all permutations gave that big of a LOD score, the p-value will be 1.

karl

messages.body_plain:

I saw an earlier discussion in this group and I was looking for it but can't find it again. It was linked to CIM results changing each time you run CIM(). The LOD scores are quite stable but change a little on each run (~0.5 LOD). Although, QTL locations are stable. I was just interested in what causes this. Is it something to do with the co-variate positioning?

Many thanks.

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] CIM LOD scores
messages.body_plain:
In the cim() function implemented within R/qtl, we rely on a single imputation at the markers to fill in any missing data prior to running forward selection to identify marker covariates. This introduces randomness.

I recommend using the mqm functions, or stepwiseqtl(), rather than cim().

karl

messages.subject: setting maxdist threshold in cleanGeno
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I was wondering if anyone had thoughts setting the threshold for cleanGeno.

Say I'm working with a backcross and I know the species has high cross over interference could I set the threshold higher?

What about species where crossover interference is very low? Is the maxdist threshold valuable at all for those species?

Am I completely wrong to think that the level of cross over interference might be relevant to setting this threshold?

I appreciate your thoughts,

-Matthew

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] setting maxdist threshold in cleanGeno
messages.body_plain:
Yes, if crossover interference is high, then maxdist could be set higher.
There's a trade-off between leaving in genotypes that are in error and omitting genotypes that are really correct.

Personally, I no longer try to clean up the genotypes. I want to identify and omit markers that are particularly badly behaved, but mostly I rely on error.prob in calc.genoprob() and est.map() to smooth over any genotyping errors.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] setting maxdist threshold in cleanGeno
messages.body_plain:
If you have low-density markers, it’s difficult to tell whether a particular genotype is an error. You can see that there are more double-crossovers then there should be, but you can’t tell which ones are errors.

If you have high-density markers, there will be more errors than you can carefully consider, individually.

But really, the things is that we’re not trying to determine the genotypes but rather to map QTL or to estimate a genetic map, and for those tasks it’s perfectly fine to just leave the errors in and use methods that are tolerant to the presence of errors.

karl
